title: The AI app builder your team trusts has a root-level backdoor
key_facts: VulnCheck began seeing continuous exploitation attempts against internet-facing Langflow on 29 Aug 2026
CVE-2026-0768 has a CVSS score of 9.8 and sits in a validate endpoint that passes submitted code to Python's exec()
In many default deployments no authentication is needed, and code runs as root
Attackers look for .env files, SSH keys, OpenAI API keys, AWS credentials and database credentials
Over 360 exploitation attempts logged on VulnCheck's UK honeypots; the number of successful attacks is unknown
Twelve Langflow flaws exploited in the wild in 2026 against one before 2026
The flaw is patched and the fix is available
quote_evidence: That number reflects observed attempts against instrumented systems.
CVE-2026-0768 is patched and the fix is available.
why_it_matters_hint: AI workflow platforms are becoming targets for credential theft.
notes: Read in full. It is a contributed opinion piece, not CSO staff reporting; the underlying exploitation started on 29 Aug 2026, so the item is older news re-dated.
